column1: An influential study by Nicholas Bloom and John Van Reenen documents the importance of good management, as well as some of the reasons that not all firms have it. Bloom and Van Reenen began by surveying 732 medium-sized manufacturing firms in four nations: the United States, the United Kingdom, France, and Germany. They asked various questions about how firms were managed and then graded each firm on how well it conformed to best practices. For example, a firm that said it promoted employees on the basis of performance was graded higher than one that said it promoted employees on the basis of how long they had been at the firm.
